slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every positive integer x. Diamond of x is three x when x is odd, and x squared minus twelve when x is even. Given: diamond of x is equal to twenty-four. x is equal to what?
Conditions again, but backwards. They give the result. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, two cases, and then plugging in the answers.
[short pause] We don't know if x is odd or even, so try both rules. The odd rule, three x is twenty-four, so x is eight. But eight is even, and an even number never uses the odd rule. Throw it out.

The even rule, x squared minus twelve is twenty-four, so x squared is thirty-six. x is positive, so six. And six is even, it fits. Choice number two is our answer. The traps are eight, and six or eight.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. What's different? We put each offered x into the operation, so the condition is checked for us. Eight is even, sixty-four minus twelve, fifty-two. Not twenty-four. Out.
Six is even, thirty-six minus twelve, twenty-four. Found it. Choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
